01.reason: After the custom of costly burials, Rabban Gamliel acts once (has himself buried in linen) and the whole people follow him, so something happens and the world changes. Rav Pappa's remark is an appended comment.

02.reason: Abaye's tenant asks, Abaye rules, Rav Yosef corrects him, and Abaye runs three parasangs after the tenant and fails to catch him. That is a sequence of events with consequences.

03.reason: Two short incidents: a man does a judge a small favour, and Ameimar and then Mar Ukva respond by disqualifying themselves. Something happens and a rabbi responds.

04.reason: An institutional history of how the priestly court changed the widow's ketubah amount. It has no particular incident or person, and serves as a reconstruction of legislation.

05.reason: Purely legal discussion of hypothetical cases. No event is narrated.

06.reason: A particular woman owes an oath, Rav Hisda's daughter testifies that she is suspect, and Rava reverses the oath. An incident followed by a ruling.

07.reason: A teaching exchange between Rav Yehuda and his son: speech only, with nothing happening beyond the remark, and the Gemara's harmonization follows.

08.reason: Rabbi Simlai's remark to his host is speech only, with no conflict and no event. It is cited as legal evidence.

09.reason: A certain man betroths with a myrtle mat, bystanders object, he changes his declaration, she takes it in silence, and Rava rules. An incident followed by a ruling.

10.reason: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa delays the Angel of Death, then argues with him. At his death a pillar of fire appears, and Rabbi Alexandri makes it depart. A full narrative; the Abaye and Rav Adda exchange is appended commentary.

11.reason: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak juggles myrtle at weddings and Rabbi Zeira objects. At his death a pillar of fire appears, and Rabbi Zeira reverses his judgment. Conflict, an event and a change.

12.reason: Rav Avya's wife's ketubah is lost and the couple come before Rav Yosef. Abaye objects to his ruling, and Rav Yosef tells them to write a new one. An incident followed by a ruling.

13.reason: After a habitual frame, a one-time event follows: Yehuda is delayed, Rabbi Yannai declares him dead, and he dies.

14.reason: Embedded in the letter is an incident: a man lovesick for a woman wanted to leave the Land, heard this teaching and stayed, suffering until he died. The rest of the letter is advice.

15.reason: Rav Yehuda's practice of struggling to read, followed by Ulla's advice: speech with no conflict and nothing following.

16.reason: Legal dialectic that only alludes to the David and Bathsheba incident; no story is narrated.

17.reason: Academic legal argument. Rav Hiyya bar Avin's recollection is part of the debate, not a narrated event.

18.reason: A bare report that Rabbi was moved to Tzippori when he fell ill, cited to resolve a contradiction. Nothing follows from it.

19.reason: Rav Aha bar Yaakov sends his son to study, then goes himself. Abaye denies him lodging, and he defeats the seven-headed demon. A full narrative.

20.reason: A certain man is punctured by a thorn and later has children. Shmuel sends the case to Rav, who responds. An incident followed by a ruling.

21.reason: A man helps Shmuel off the ferry, and Shmuel learns he has a case and disqualifies himself. Something happens and a rabbi responds.

22.reason: Rabbi Evyatar meets Elijah and challenges him, and Elijah resolves the challenge. A post-biblical rabbi's encounter with Elijah is in scope; segment 2 is exegetical setup.

23.reason: Ravina recites the blessing at the betrothal, confident the match will hold, and then the other family retracts. An event with a reversal. The Rav Tahlifa line is a bare report with a ruling.

24.reason: A beautiful woman claims to be betrothed in order to deter suitors, later betroths herself, is questioned by the Sages and explains, and a ruling follows.

25.reason: A widow is refused by Rabba bar Rav Huna and curses him. He overturns his chair, yet still falls ill. Conflict, actions and a consequence.
